newsitem.title: USA: House passes balanced budget legislation.
newsitem.headline: House passes balanced budget legislation.

text.p: The U.S. House of Representatives on Wednesday passed balanced budget legislation that supporters said would break Washington's deficit spending habit and boost the economy.
A day after President Bill Clinton and congressional leaders announced a five-year budget agreement, House Republican leaders pushed the measure to the floor where it won a bipartisan majority.

The measure passed by 346 votes to 85. It was opposed by conservative Republicans who felt it did not go far enough and liberal Democrats, including Minority Leader Dick Gephardt, who thought it went too far.

"(This) represents the dawning of a new era. It's an era where we recognise the limits of government and begin one mroe time to count on...the innovation, the creativity and the pure energy of the American people," said Budget Committee Chairman John Kasich, an Ohio Republican.

Some Democrats complained voters had been hoodwinked. They praised a $24 billion children's health initiative in the measure, but said Medicare was being cut too deeply in order to finance tax cuts that would mainly benefit the better off.

The legislation reduces federal spending by about $130 billion over the next five years and calls on Congress to find an additional $140 billion in cuts through annual appopriations bills. As part of the overall budget deal, the House and Senate will also vote on companion tax cutting legislation.
